title: What AI can run in a short-term rental, what it should only draft, and what needs a person
summary: Sort every hosting job by what happens if it goes wrong: run what one message can undo, draft what spends money, and keep the irreversible with a person.
body_markdown:
[All posts](https://prohost.ai/blog)


**"AI co-host" sounds like one thing. In practice the work of hosting splits into three piles. Some of it AI can run on its own today: the Wi-Fi question at 2 a.m., the check-in message, scheduling the cleaning. Some of it AI should only draft, and wait for you: a refund, a discount, a reply to an angry guest. And some of it needs a person no matter how good the AI gets: deciding to cancel a stay, hiring a cleaner, standing in the doorway when a pipe bursts. Here's how we sort every hosting job into those three piles, and how to set your tools to match.**


## Key takeaways


- **Run:** high-volume, low-risk, reversible work with a clear right answer. Routine guest questions, scheduled messages, cleaning schedules, lock codes, guest reviews, task creation.
- **Draft:** anything that spends money, makes an exception to a rule, or speaks for you when the stakes are high. Refunds, discounts, early check-in conflicts, replies to complaints, public responses to bad reviews.
- **Person:** decisions that are irreversible or involve someone's safety, livelihood or legal standing. Cancellations, emergencies, hiring and paying vendors, permits and taxes.
- **The sorting rule is about consequences, not difficulty.** A hard question with a reversible answer can be run. An easy question with an irreversible answer can't.
- **Good tools let you set the line per topic.** In ProhostAI, Autopilot sends only above a confidence threshold you set, topic by topic, and holds "approval required" topics for you ([Autopilot](https://prohost.ai/features/autopilot) ).

## Where we're coming from


We host in Hawaii, the Smokies and Joshua Tree, and we run that hosting on ProhostAI, so we live with these lines every day. Before ProhostAI I spent 6 years at Airbnb as a staff data scientist on the hosting team. What carries over from that work is a habit of asking which mistakes are cheap to undo. A wrong Wi-Fi answer is fixed in one message. A wrong cancellation is a fee, a blocked calendar and a guest with nowhere to sleep ([Airbnb host cancellation policy](https://www.airbnb.com/help/article/990) ). Those two shouldn't run through the same setting.


## The sorting rule


For any hosting job, ask three questions:


1. **Can it be undone in one message?** If yes, it's a candidate to run.
2. **Does it spend money or make an exception?** If yes, draft it.
3. **Could it hurt someone, or can it not be taken back?** If yes, a person decides.


The rule doesn't care how hard the job is. "Is the pool heated in October, and how warm does it get?" is a harder question than "Can I get a refund?", but the first is reversible and the second spends money.

## Pile 2: what AI should only draft


These are jobs where the AI does most of the work, gathering context and writing the reply, and a person presses send.


- **Refunds and partial refunds.** Money leaves. Draft the reply and the amount, then approve it.
- **Discounts and price exceptions.** A discount for one guest becomes the expected price for the next. Draft, then decide.
- **Early check-in and late checkout when the calendar is tight.** The AI can check the cleaning schedule and propose an answer. You confirm if it means asking a cleaner to move.
- **Replies to complaints.** When a guest is upset, the first reply sets the tone of the review. Autopilot escalates conversations where a guest sounds frustrated, with an optional short holding reply so nobody waits in silence ([Autopilot](https://prohost.ai/features/autopilot) ).
- **Public responses to negative reviews.** Everyone who reads your listing reads this. Draft it, sleep on it, send it.
- **Review disputes.** The[dispute builder](https://prohost.ai/tools/review-dispute-builder) reads the stay record and drafts the case for Airbnb's form. You file it yourself.
- **Anything to owners.** Statements, repair approvals, a hard conversation about performance.


In ProhostAI the mechanism is the same everywhere: mark a topic **approval required** and Autopilot drafts those replies and waits for you while the rest keep sending.[AI workflows](https://prohost.ai/ai-agent-workflows) let you decide which steps run automatically and which pause for approval.[AI employees](https://prohost.ai/discover/ai-employees) bring their work to you as approval requests when it crosses a line you set.


## Pile 3: what needs a person


- **Cancelling a stay.** It's irreversible for the guest and expensive for you: Airbnb's fee runs from 10% to 50% of the nights not stayed, with a $50 minimum ([Airbnb](https://www.airbnb.com/help/article/990) ).
- **Emergencies.** Fire, flood, injury, a guest who can't get in at midnight in winter. The AI can triage, notify your on-call person and keep the guest informed. A person decides and shows up.
- **Safety and screening calls.** Whether to accept a booking that worries you.
- **Hiring, firing and paying people.** Cleaners, handymen, co-hosts. Software can schedule and pay on a rule you set; choosing the person is yours.
- **Permits, taxes and legal.** Every county rule, every tax filing. Our[Hawaii taxes guide](https://prohost.ai/blog/hawaii-short-term-rental-taxes-and-county-rules) is an example of how much of this is judgment.
- **Your pricing strategy.** A pricing tool sets the daily rate. You set the floor, the ceiling and what kind of host you are.


## A sorting sheet you can copy


```text
AI SORTING SHEET: RUN / DRAFT / PERSON


For each job in your week, answer:
1. Can a mistake be undone in one message?        yes / no
2. Does it spend money or make an exception?       yes / no
3. Could it hurt someone or not be taken back?    yes / no


1 = yes, 2 = no, 3 = no   -> RUN    (autopilot / schedule)
2 = yes, 3 = no           -> DRAFT  (approval required)
3 = yes                   -> PERSON (AI can notify and prepare, not decide)


Job                          | 1 | 2 | 3 | Pile
Wi-Fi / parking questions    |   |   |   |
Check-in message             |   |   |   |
Early check-in request       |   |   |   |
Refund request               |   |   |   |
Complaint reply              |   |   |   |
Review response (negative)   |   |   |   |
Cancellation                 |   |   |   |
Lockout at night             |   |   |   |


```

## FAQ


**Is it safe to let AI answer guests on its own?** For routine questions with a threshold and a short delay, yes. Keep money, exceptions and complaints on approval.


**What's the difference between an AI co-host and Autopilot?** "AI co-host" is a marketing term for many things. What matters is which jobs the AI runs, which it drafts, and which it hands to you. Ask any vendor for that list.


**Should AI ever cancel a reservation?** No. Cancellations are irreversible and carry Airbnb fees and penalties. AI can prepare the case; a person decides.


**Can AI handle an emergency?** It can triage, notify your on-call person and keep the guest updated. A person handles the emergency.


**How do I know where to set the confidence threshold?** Use your own history. In ProhostAI, the threshold setting shows how many past messages each level would have automated.


## The takeaway


Don't ask whether AI can do a job. Ask what happens if it gets the job wrong. If the answer is "one more message," let it run. If the answer is "money or an exception," let it draft. If the answer is "someone gets hurt or it can't be undone," keep it with a person, and let the AI make that person faster.
